_comment: Source of truth for Wren's App Store listing in its primary language.
Every other locale is translated from this file, so edit it here and
re-run the push rather than editing anything in App Store Connect by hand.
Apple's limits: name 30, subtitle 30, promotionalText 170, keywords 100,
description 4000. The push script checks all of them before sending.
Shared fields — name and the two URLs — come from common.json.
subtitle: Place lists into map guides
promotionalText: Share a reel or a post to Wren and it reads the places out of it, ready to check and save to your map. Screenshots and exported lists work too.
description:
Someone sends you a reel. Five places you have to eat at in Rome, a rooftop bar in Lisbon, a bookshop down an alley in Tokyo. You mean to remember. By Thursday it is gone.

Wren catches them — off a screenshot, out of a list another app exported, or from a guide you already keep — and puts them where you will be standing when you need them.

FOUR WAYS IN

Places do not only arrive as screenshots, so there are four ways to hand them over. All of them end in the same place: a guide in Apple Maps.

1. FROM A REEL OR A POST. Share it to Wren and the places are read out of it. Wren's server fetches the post, reads it and discards it — the video never reaches your phone. Paid, with 250 posts a month.

2. FROM SCREENSHOTS. One tap per place, from a reel, a post, a message from a friend, or a photographed page of a guidebook. Text recognition runs on your phone, so the screenshots stay there. Wren also reads the caption to work out which city you are looking at, and asks you to confirm it.

3. FROM A FILE. A list exported from another app — CSV, KML, KMZ, GPX, GeoJSON, or a Google Takeout export of your saved places. Where the file carries coordinates, each place is looked up near its own, so a list spanning three cities resolves correctly rather than being dragged towards one of them.

4. FROM A GUIDE YOU ALREADY HAVE. Share a guide out of Apple Maps, paste the link into Wren, and it reads the places already in it. Newly found places sit alongside them, and one guide is made holding both.

THEN YOU CHECK IT

Every place shows what was read beside what was matched, so a wrong match is obvious rather than confident. Anything not found — or found wrongly — can be searched again by hand. Nothing is written to Apple Maps until you say so.

What comes out is not a copy of your places in another app. It is an actual guide, in the Maps you already use, on every device signed in to your Apple Account. About a hundred and fifty places fit in one guide; beyond that Wren splits them into numbered guides and tells you before it does, rather than quietly dropping the ones that would not fit.

ANYWHERE, NOT JUST RESTAURANTS

Restaurants and bars, certainly. Also viewpoints, markets, hotels, galleries, shops, trailheads, beaches and the odd petrol station someone insists does the best coffee for fifty miles. Anywhere with a name and a location.

NO ACCOUNT, NO SIGN-IN

Wren has no account and reads nothing from yours. Screenshots are read on your device and are never uploaded.

Three things leave your phone, and only when you ask: the name of a place, sent to Apple Maps so it can be found, exactly as the Maps app does; a shared guide link, sent to Apple to be expanded; and the link to a reel or post you share, sent to Wren's own server, which fetches that post, reads the names out of it and discards it. Nothing about the post is kept.

FREE, WITH OPTIONAL PURCHASES

Guides of up to three places are free, for good, and so is reading a screenshot. Two one-time purchases: one removes the three-place cap and lets you add to a guide you already have, the other reads places out of a shared post. Buying both together costs less than buying them apart. No subscription, and everything restores on your other devices.

WHAT APPLE ALLOWS, PLAINLY

Apple Maps offers no way to add to an existing guide from outside the app, so combining makes a new guide holding the old places and the new ones together — Wren keeps them, so it can be made again in a tap.

reviewNotes:
WHERE THE IN-APP PURCHASES ARE

From a cold start, nothing added, no account needed:

    1. Open Wren.
    2. Tap the three-dot menu at the TOP RIGHT.
    3. Tap "Guides of any size", or "Places from a post".

Either opens a purchase sheet with the StoreKit price and "Restore a previous
purchase". Three non-consumables:

    ...littlebird.unlimited       guides of any size
    ...littlebird.everything      both, for somebody who owns neither
    ...littlebird.reels.upgrade   adds reading posts to an owner of "unlimited"

The sheet shows what is LEFT to buy: owning nothing offers "everything",
owning "unlimited" offers the upgrade.

iPhone-only (TARGETED_DEVICE_FAMILY = 1); same menu on iPad.

NEW IN 2.1.9

A post is now read free three times (was once) before the purchase sheet;
the purchase sheet leads with the places already found; and the app posts
anonymous step counts (see the last list) to Wren's own server.

MEASUREMENT SDKS (FROM 2.1.8)

Wren includes two advertising-measurement SDKs, to measure its own adverts:
Meta's (FBSDKCoreKit 18.1.1) and, new in 2.1.8, TikTok's (TikTokBusinessSDK
1.7.2). Both send automatic events only (install, app open, App Store
purchase; TikTok also a day-2 return and, if TikTok enables it, crash
reports). Wren adds no events of its own.

One ATT prompt, shown just after first launch, covers both. Declining changes
nothing in the app, and the IDFA is sent only if tracking is allowed. In UK
and EEA storefronts neither SDK is started at all unless tracking is allowed.
TikTok's own ATT prompt and SKAdNetwork handling are switched off.
The privacy label and privacy policy were updated to match.

To let Apple attribute installs from ads (SKAdNetwork / AdAttributionKit),
Wren calls updatePostbackConversionValue(0, coarseValue: .low) once at first
launch, under the same UK/EEA rule. Postback copies go to spencerfields.com
(NSAdvertisingAttributionReportEndpoint, AttributionCopyEndpoint).

NOTIFICATION AFTER SHARING

The share extension schedules a local notification once a reel or post is
handed to Wren; tapping it opens the app. Local only (UNUserNotificationCenter):
no push, no server. Provisional permission is requested on first launch.

READING A SHARED POST

A share sheet hands over a URL, never the media, so the link goes to Wren's
server (a Cloudflare Worker), which fetches the post, has a model read the
place names, and returns the NAMES as text. Nothing about the post is retained.
The first post is read free (one per Apple Account, via AppTransaction; needs
iOS 18.4); the purchase sheet appears on the second.

To test without an Instagram account, share this public post to Wren, or use
"Add", "From a link":

    https://www.instagram.com/p/DcZzVx4Da6a/

Ten castle hotels in seven countries. When asked which city, tap "Search
anywhere".

IF YOU WOULD RATHER NOT TRANSACT

A complimentary code unlocks everything. Please use it only AFTER looking at
the purchase sheets, because entering it removes them. Long-press the "Wren"
title at the top left, then enter:

    7QFG-7FVY-QXP6-2AT6

WHAT LEAVES THE DEVICE, IN FULL

    * A place name, to Apple, for MapKit.
    * A pasted Apple Maps guide link, to Apple, to be expanded.
    * A complimentary code and a random device identifier, to Wren's code
      server, only when a code is entered.
    * A reel or post link, to Wren's reel server, only when one is shared,
      with a proof of purchase or Apple's AppTransaction.
    * Install, app-open and purchase events, to Meta and TikTok (see above):
      outside the UK/EEA from first launch; the IDFA only if tracking is
      allowed.

    * Anonymous step counts (e.g. "paywall_shown"), to Wren's own server,
      with platform, app version and language: no identifier, nothing
      stored on the device, not tracking.

Screenshots are read on the device and never leave it.
